directions.shared_object: A live assurance premise, defeater or evidence gap actually constraining structural evolution.
directions.guard: The structural decision consumes a specific relevant claim obligation or challenge from an actual assurance argument. A useful partial constraint can matter before the whole safety or economic claim is established.
directions.source_contribution: The argument identifies which scope, assumption, evidence dependency or known doubt must be addressed for the candidate.
directions.receiving_consequence: Work can preserve a consequential invariant, repair or narrow a claim, use an adequate alternative or decline speculative restructuring when the actual burden is unjustified.
directions.remaining_premises: The argument may be biased or stale; its authority and form do not make its premises true. Whole risk and net benefit remain open unless separately supported.
directions.positive_witness: The explicit boundary failure rules out the same-scoped preservation claim; source analysis and a justified no-change path remain available. AC02 retains untested intended-use premises instead of laundering them through finite equality.
directions.nontrigger_or_counterexample: A post-hoc persuasive case or irrelevant milestone demand is not a credible technical constraint. Low-risk stable work need not create a monolithic assurance dossier.
directions.cheap_alternative_and_removal: A concise current evidence/claim summary or direct technical challenge can suffice. Remove a real relevant premise and the change loses a constraint; remove paperwork while the premise survives does not destroy the function.
directions.reentry: New defeater, changed claim/context, actual cost or evidence availability.

directions.shared_object: A material anomaly or exception exposed or affected by structural work, tied to the correct candidate and claim.
directions.guard: An actual problem/disposition inquiry consumes a structural failure, residual limitation or correction result. A failed experimental candidate is not automatically a deployed incident.
directions.source_contribution: The changed artifact and its scoped observation identify what failed, which behavior and configuration are implicated and whether a claimed correction actually addresses them.
directions.receiving_consequence: The problem record can retain the unresolved state, distinguish candidate from predecessor or reject closure based solely on a green summary or new ticket status.
directions.remaining_premises: Severity, causal diagnosis, disposition authority, accepted residuals and actual operational impact remain separate. A source transformation is not a verified fix of every affected system.
directions.positive_witness: V3 fails at4 and V5 misses logbook at3; complete alternatives have separately identified evidence. A predecessor-only result cannot establish closure on V2 merely through an identity substitution.
directions.nontrigger_or_counterexample: No material anomaly or disposition consumer gives no such interface. A nominal pass or deletion of a failing expectation cannot close the original preservation claim.
directions.cheap_alternative_and_removal: An identified issue plus adequate regression evidence can suffice. Remove anomaly/configuration correspondence and closure loses its referent; remove a discrepancy board while accountable tracking remains and the function survives.
directions.reentry: Changed anomaly, candidate, residual, evidence, severity or closure basis.

directions.shared_object: An actual anomaly, accepted exception or corrective obligation consumed when choosing structural work and verification.
directions.guard: A relevant identified problem or residual condition changes the structural choice, preservation target or required closure evidence. The input can matter before root cause or full corrective effectiveness is known.
directions.source_contribution: The record supplies affected scope, current status, relevant evidence and the actual disposition limit; it keeps a known defect visible through a rewrite.
directions.receiving_consequence: Work can prioritize a real friction source, preserve a necessary exception, distinguish a bug fix from behavior-preserving refactoring or require evidence on the successor instead of closing by label.
directions.remaining_premises: An accepted waiver is scoped and must be real; none is executed here. Repairing behavior may be appropriate but must not be mislabeled as preserving the same old behavior.
directions.positive_witness: C28 distinguishes R4 preservation from the later R3 change and shows partial/direct/shared results separately. Adequate current evidence can settle the bounded technical question without another run; no ticket authority or causal incident diagnosis is modeled.
directions.nontrigger_or_counterexample: A stale backlog item or unrelated waiver cannot constrain the current claim. Changing the criterion to hide failure while claiming unchanged R4 is invalid; a genuinely changed obligation must be explicit.
directions.cheap_alternative_and_removal: A tracked issue, concise exception record and adequate current test or analysis can suffice. Remove the real unresolved condition and structural work may silently erase it; remove ceremonial triage without losing the condition and no loss follows.
directions.reentry: Changed disposition, scope, requirement, source, residual or contrary closure evidence.
